## Technical analysis (Sunday June 28 — pre-market review, US markets closed)

**No US trading June 28 (Sunday).** Last confirmed close: $192.53 (June 26).

**Stop Day 1 unchanged:** $192.53 < $195. Day 1 active. Day 2 = June 29 US close. Two consecutive closes below $195 = mandatory full exit.

**Samsung Blue House announcement (dominant catalyst):** Samsung $646B ($226B AI data centers, $194B semiconductor plants) + SK Hynix ADR $29.4B announced jointly at Blue House June 29. The $226B AI data center commitment is the most powerful external demand-side validation of NVDA's hyperscaler AI infrastructure thesis ever announced in a single corporate event. Direct read-through: at current GPU cluster pricing, $226B in Samsung AI data centers implies 40,000–80,000+ NVDA B200/B300 GPU clusters over the investment horizon.

**Stop reset probability:** Pre-weekend ~40%; post-Samsung announcement ~60–65%. The Samsung catalyst provides the KOSPI/US premarket risk-on driver that was absent over the prior weekend. A June 29 KST open with KOSPI +4–5% (Samsung demand read-through) and SK Hynix above ₩2,800,000 (ADR underwriter stabilization) creates a high-probability NVDA premarket gap above $195.

**Distribution ceiling unchanged:** $202.17 (June 26 Russell Reconstitution open) remains the confirmed institutional selling level. Sellers who absorbed $334B in passive reconstitution demand will need a macro regime shift before covering. Samsung announcement is a demand catalyst, not a supply-side change.

**Regime gates:** Unchanged (VIX 18.41, DXY 101.27, SPX 7,354 / 106 pts below floor). Samsung announcement could compress VIX, narrow SPX gap, and modestly weaken DXY on KRW strength — but full gate clearance is not expected in a single Monday session.

so_what.line: If you hold NVDA, the framework is unchanged — HOLD on low conviction with the $195 stop clock running — but Samsung's $226B AI data center commitment announced Monday morning is the most powerful demand-side catalyst of the cycle and materially raises the odds the stop resets rather than triggers on June 29.
so_what.bull: Samsung committing $226 billion to AI data centers is the demand validation you own NVDA for — that level of national-strategic capex runs on NVDA silicon.
so_what.bear: Still below the $195 stop line in a breached-regime environment; Samsung's data centers are a 10-year plan, not a June 29 revenue event, and one bad NFP print still triggers the forced exit.
